reason: The cited evidence shows DIC used for strain measurement (E3) and synchrotron imaging mentioned only in the hypothesis, not in evidence. No evidence supports real-time dynamic recalibration, the claimed 5% error margin, or the 7× speedup. E1 and E4 are unrelated to the proposed method, and E2 describes MD simulations with high strain rates, conflicting with the hypothesis's real-time calibration premise.
premises: Real-time high-speed DIC can capture evolving strain fields during tensile testing of HfNbTiVAl10.
Synchrotron imaging can simultaneously capture crack initiation and propagation in this alloy.
Dynamic recalibration of a multi-scale simulation using real-time imaging data improves prediction accuracy.
This data–simulation feedback loop enables prediction of Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior within 5% error.
The approach achieves up to 7× faster prediction speed compared to established simulations.
